sentence: the Sun slides its own width every minute (12 h), 16 s (3 h), 8 s (1.5 h)
claim: The Sun's apparent motion is 360° divided by the day length: 0.5° per minute at a 12 h day, 2° per minute at 3 h and 4° per minute at 1.5 h. The Sun's disk is about 0.53° wide, so it moves its own width every 64 s, 16 s and 8 s.

sentence: Standing on the equator, the ground carries you around at about sixteen hundred and seventy kilometers an hour.
claim: The ground at the equator moves at about 1,674 km/h (465 m/s): one trip around the equator divided by the length of a day. That is about 1/17 of the speed needed to orbit.
note: DERIVATION: arithmetic only; not read from any page. OPEN until a person re-does the sum.
derivation: v = 2 pi R / T = 465 m/s = 1,674 km/h from R = 6,378 km and T = 23.934 h; and 7.9 km/s / 0.465 km/s = 17.
